description: Build a Python daemon 'mcp_directory_ingestor.py' that ingests the Anthropic official MCP reference list from modelcontextprotocol.io/servers. This is PILOT MODE for Phase II of Sentinel Roadmap v2. The module must: (1) fetch https://modelcontextprotocol.io/servers exactly once per invocation, with User-Agent 'zo-sentinel/1.0 (mcp-trust-intelligence)' and From header 'hello@zocomputer.io'. (2) Parse the HTML to extract MCP entries -- look for package names, github repo URLs, brief descriptions. Anthropic publishes this as a structured page; use BeautifulSoup or html.parser. (3) For each extracted entry, attempt to match against existing rows in mcp_server_registry via: exact name match, name-modulo-scope match (@modelcontextprotocol/server-X equivalent to server-X), or repo URL match (normalize by stripping .git, www., trailing slashes). (4) Write matched entries into mcp_directory_mentions table with directory_name='anthropic_reference'. (5) Write unmatched entries (new MCPs Anthropic lists but we don't have) into mcp_discovery_candidates table for operator review -- DO NOT auto-insert into mcp_server_registry. (6) Emit a summary log line with counts: fetched, matched, new_candidates. (7) Include a __main__ block that calls ingest_anthropic_reference() once and exits. The module exposes functions: ingest_anthropic_reference(), _normalize_name(), _normalize_url(), _match_to_registry(name, url). Pilot success criteria: fetches in under 30s, parses at least 15 entries, matches at least 10 to existing registry.
context:
CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION RULES:

1. Use WriteService at http://127.0.0.1:8772 for ALL database operations. Never connect directly to DuckDB.

2. For NEW tables (mcp_directory_mentions, mcp_discovery_candidates): use the /execute endpoint with explicit INSERT ON CONFLICT, NOT the /write endpoint. WriteService /write auto-injects an 'id' column which breaks tables with different PK structures. This lesson was learned the hard way on 2026-04-19 with the ecosystems_metadata_fetcher.

3. Schema to create if not present (idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS):

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_directory_mentions (
  id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  server_id VARCHAR,
  directory_name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  mention_url VARCHAR,
  mention_context VARCHAR,
  mention_rank INTEGER,
  first_seen TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  last_seen TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mcp_discovery_candidates (
  id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  candidate_name VARCHAR NOT NULL,
  candidate_url VARCHAR,
  discovered_in_directory VARCHAR,
  first_seen TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  reviewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  promoted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE
);

4. Heartbeat: POST to WriteService /write with table='service_health', rows={'service':'mcp_directory_ingestor', 'last_heartbeat': ISO-8601 UTC, 'status':'running'}

5. Use requests library, NOT urllib. Timeout 15s on fetch. On non-200, log and exit cleanly with exit code 0 (not a crash -- just try again next cycle).

6. Parsing defense: if parse finds fewer than 5 entries, log WARNING 'anthropic_reference parser: page structure may have changed' and exit without writing. Page structure changes are real; fail safe rather than write bad data.

7. DO NOT execute in a loop. This is a ONE-SHOT pilot. Single invocation, single fetch, write, exit. A daemon wrapper will invoke it daily later.

8. Log format: '%(asctime)s [mcp_directory_ingestor] %(levelname)s: %(message)s' at INFO level to stdout.

9. Identifier generation: for id fields, use int(hashlib.md5(f'{directory_name}:{candidate_name}'.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % (2**31) -- deterministic so re-runs upsert instead of duplicating.

10. Exit codes: 0=success, 1=fetch failure, 2=parse failure, 3=write failure. Match with patch_status conventions.
